content: 1. Osimertinib and Strong CYP3A4 Inhibitors: Avoid coadministration of osimertinib with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If no alternative treatment is available, closely monitor the patient for adverse effects. 2. Cobicistat and Ospemifene: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ospemifene by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 3. Oxcarbazepine and Cobicistat: Oxcarbazepine decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. If coadministration is necessary, monitor for reduced virologic response. 4. Cobicistat and Oxycodone: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of oxycodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely for signs of respiratory depression and sedation. 5. Fentanyl and CYP3A4 Inhibitors: If coadministration of fentanyl with CYP3A4 inhibitors is necessary, monitor the patient frequently for respiratory depression and sedation. Adjust the fentanyl dose as needed until stable drug effects are achieved. 6. Cobicistat and Ozanimod: Cobicistat increases the toxicity of ozanimod by increasing the exposure of its active metabolites (CC112273 and CC1084037). Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 7. Cobicistat and Paclitaxel: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of paclitaxel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Cobicistat and Pacritinib: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of pacritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated due to the risk of increased toxicity. 9. Cobicistat and Palbociclib: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of palbociclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the palbociclib dose to 75 mg/day. 10. Cobicistat and Palovarotene: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of palovarotene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 11. Cobicistat and Panobinostat: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of panobinostat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the starting dose of panobinostat to 10 mg if coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 12. Cobicistat and Paricalcitol: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of paricalcitol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Cobicistat and Paroxetine: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of paroxetine through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 inhibition. Carefully titrate the dose of paroxetine to achieve the desired effect, starting with the lowest feasible dose. Monitor the response during coadministration with cobicistat. 14. Cobicistat and Pazopanib: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of pazopanib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 15. Cobicistat and Pemigatinib: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of pemigatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pemigatinib dose as per the drug monograph. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, resume the previous pemigatinib dose. 16. Cobicistat and Perampanel: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of perampanel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 17. Cobicistat and Perphenazine: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of perphenazine through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 inhibition. A dose reduction of antipsychotics metabolized by CYP3A or CYP2D6 may be necessary upon coadministration. Monitor closely. 18. Cobicistat and Pexidartinib: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of pexidartinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pexidartinib dose as per the drug monograph. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, resume the previous pexidartinib dose. 19. Phenobarbital and Cobicistat: Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is necessary, monitor for reduced virologic response. 20. Phenytoin and Cobicistat: Phenytoin decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is necessary, monitor for reduced virologic response.
